title: Trident Shipping — Private Deploy proposal: capacity planning, TF rollout notes
content:
Purpose:
Draft playbook for Trident Shipping Co. private deployment (VPC + on-prem hybrid). Covers capacity assumptions, recommended TF modules/ordering, rollout strategy, cutover checklist, and known risks/questions for pre-sales/ops handoff.

Summary (one-liner):
Provide a hardened private inference stack for Trident (logistics optimization and document ingestion pipelines) with predictable SLOs: 99.9% up at p95 latency <= 180ms for small-model routes, burstable to hosted for peak loads.

Customer context / constraints:
- Trident runs core dispatch/ETA features in Europe and APAC regions; requires data residency in EU region for PII-enriched payloads.
- On-prem rack in Amsterdam colo for low-latency local inference; cloud VPC in GCP europe-west1 for model orchestration and ephemeral workers.
- Security: customer KMS, strict egress rules (only to Redwood control-plane endpoints and specific S3 buckets), quarterly vulnerability scans, FIPS-compliant crypto optional.
- Budget sensitivity: initial committed capacity target ~ 2M tokens/day, expected to grow 3x in 12 months.
- Existing infra: customer has Kubernetes (k8s 1.25) and a private artifact registry.

SLO/throughput targets used for sizing (assumptions):
- Baseline traffic: 20 reqs/s average across 4 primary routes.
- Avg tokens per request: 80 tokens (input + generation).
- Peak traffic: 120 reqs/s sustained for 10m every hour (batchy surge).
- Expected average token throughput: 20k tokens/sec at peak.
- Latency targets: p50 < 90ms (small 7B-like models), p95 < 180ms for targeted routes.

Model mix & serving strategy:
- Primary models: open-7B quantized variant for most routes; fallbacks to higher-capacity 13B quantized variant for long-context workflows.
- Use dedicated local pool for the 7B variants (low-latency), reserve a small pool of 13B for scheduled heavy tasks.
- Enable prefix/KV caching on common prompts (shipment-status) to reduce repeated token compute.

Recommended hardware footprint (initial):
- Local on-prem (primary low-latency pool): 3 x GPU nodes (NVIDIA H100L or A10G if H100 not available) each with 4x40GB GPUs (or 8x48GB A100 if customer prefers). Rationale: target continuous concurrency ~8-12 streams/node for 7B quantized workload.
- Cloud VPC pool (orchestration + burst): 2 x medium-weight GPU nodes (A100-80GB) for 13B variants and for autoscaling burst.
- Control-plane: 2 x m5.large-ish VMs in private VPC for agent/controller services, placed in different subnets for HA.
- Storage: 2TB NVMe per GPU node for model artifacts + KV cache; weekly snapshot to encrypted NFS/object-storage.
- Networking: minimum 25 Gbps NICs on GPU nodes; internal baseline throughput requirement 10 Gbps to model-store.

Why these numbers: conservative concurrency targets to meet latency SLO while leaving headroom for online quantized model memory overhead and KV cache. We purposely overspec a bit to avoid tail latency spikes during prefix-cache misses.

Terraform module guidance / ordering notes:
- Use central state (GCS backend) with encryption and a dedicated service account. Workspaces per environment (tri-prod, tri-stage).
- Modules to reuse from infra repo: module.vpc (customized peering/routing rules), module.k8s-cluster (kubeadm -> machine images with GPU drivers pre-baked), module.gpu-pool (node pools with autoscaler hooks), module/iam-and-kms, module/artifact-sync (registry mirroring), module/rdp-or-ssh-bastion.
- Minimal apply sequence (high level):
  1. bootstrap: create state buckets, IAM bindings, KMS keys (customer KMS integration note below).
  2. core-network: vpc, subnets, firewall rules (no GPU nodes yet).
  3. control-plane: VM instances for controllers, load-balancers for control-plane endpoints.
  4. k8s + drivers: cluster + GPU driver DaemonSet + node image validation.
  5. gpu-pool: node pools with taints/labels.
  6. model-store: object buckets / PVs + artifact-sync jobs.
  7. runtime-deploy: Redwood runtime containers, KV-cache, autoscaler hooks, healthchecks.
  8. security-posture: iptables, hardening, image scanning jobs.

TF module nitpicks / gotchas we saw in other customers:
- Module variable that toggles "private_gke_node_metadata" sometimes defaults to allow broader metadata access; enforce explicit false.
- GPU driver version pinning: make the driver version an explicit variable in module.gpu-pool; mismatch caused node failing to join.
- KMS integration: customer-managed key resource sometimes needs additional binding to the TF SA used by the controller; include a one-line IAM grant in module.iam-and-kms for the controller service account.
- State locking: test restore from snapshot early. We recommend retention policy to keep at least 30 days of state snapshots.

Upgrade / rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0: dry-run in staging (mirror customer workload using sampled production traces for 48h). Acceptance: tail latency in staging must be within 20% of baseline.
- Phase 1: deploy control plane and infra; smoke test endpoints, artifact sync validated.
- Phase 2: seed 1 GPU node with runtime; run canary traffic (1% of traffic) routed from prod edge to private pool. Monitor cost/latency/errors for 24h.
- Phase 3: incrementally add nodes to reach initial capacity; enable autoscaler with conservative thresholds.
- Phase 4: enable full cutover (switch routing for EU data paths), keep host fallback path enabled for non-critical routes for 72h.
- Phase 5: run full load test (production replay) for 6h, validate regression alerts and QoE metrics.

Cutover runbook (short checklist):
- Pre-cutover: verify backups, TF plan reviewed, disaster contacts ok, control-plane certs valid.
- T-2h: lock TF state, snapshot model-store, ensure healthchecks green.
- T-30m: redirect 1% traffic to canary node, verify trace IDs and fallback work.
- T+0: increase weight to 10% then 50% if no regression for 1h each.
- T+24h: metrics review and security scan.

Rollback plan:
- Immediate rollback: use routing weight to shift traffic back to hosted endpoints.
- If node-level failure: cordon+drain failed nodes and add replacement nodes from autoscaler group.
- If control-plane compromised: fail traffic to hosted and initiate incident runbook; preserve state snapshots.

Acceptance criteria / smoke tests (must pass before full cutover):
- 99.9% of p95 latency under target thresholds for canary traffic window.
- Model checksum parity between cloud and on-prem builds.
- KV-cache hit-rate >= 35% for targeted routes during replay.
- Successful KMS encryption/decryption roundtrip with customer key.

Security & compliance notes:
- KMS: we recommend using customer-managed KMS with envelope encryption; TF will reference key by resource id but SA must be explicitly granted cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter.
- Audit logs: enable VPC flow logs and control-plane audit logs forwarded to the customer's secure log sink.
- Scans: run Clair/Trivy image scans before deployment; include CVE blocking thresholds in CI.

Known risks / open questions (to resolve with Trident):
- They asked for "air-gapped mode" for an offline fallback; need to decide whether we deliver an offline bundle of runtime images + model artifacts and how updates are performed.
- Exact GPU SKU preference pending procurement timeline; H100 vs A100 availability may shift node counts.
- Will customer accept a managed bastion, or do they require fully internal-only access? network egress rules vary.
- Support windows / on-call rotation post-handoff: define SLA and escalation paths (we proposed L2 coverage 8x5 + optional 24x7).

Operational runnotes / monitoring config suggestions:
- Per-model dashboards: token/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, memory pressure, GC events, kv-cache hit rate.
- Alerts: p95>threshold for 15m, OOM/kube node eviction, model-load failures.
- Tracing: include request ID propagation and sampling at 10% with span tags recording model variant and cache-hit.

Action items / next steps:
- (Aditi) finalize the H100 vs A100 holder decision with procurement team (due 2025-11-12).
- (Liam) add explicit SA->KMS binding snippet to module.iam-and-kms and open PR in infra repo (#789).
- (Sofia) create staging replay suite from last 14 days of EU traffic; target 48h run.
- (Trident infra lead) confirm bastion preference and approval for outbound control-plane egress endpoints.

Appendix: quick TF snippet recommendations (example variables to set)
- backend: bucket = "tri-prod-terraform-state", prefix = "redwood/tri"
- module.gpu-pool: { instance_type = "nvidia-h100-48gb", desired_capacity = 3, max_size = 6, gpu_driver_version = "535.86" }
- module.iam-and-kms: { customer_kms_key = "projects/tri-prod/locations/europe/keyRings/tri/cryptoKeys/tri-key", controller_sa = "serviceAccount:infra-controller@tri-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" }

Notes to reviewer: this is intentionally conservative on capacity and TF ordering; once procurement and procurement SKU are confirmed we will re-run the capacity model with actual measured token/sec for their sampled prompt set.

End of document.
